text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KONTINENT

-- A day before he was murdered on Wednesday Bulgaria's former prime minister Andrei Lukanov has said he had incontestable evidence of corruption at the highest levels of the state, which he planned to make public by the end of the month, Loukanov's close friend and political associate Andrei Raichev said in an interview.

-- All Bulgaria's former prime ministers who were in office after the fall of the communism in 1989 will be guarded by the state services following the assasination of Andrei Lukanov, the national radio quoted the head of the National Investigation Service Boiko Rashkov as saying.
24 CHASA

-- The murder of Andrei Lukanov was linked to a report by the interior minister Nikolai Dobrev about the corruption in Bulgarian banks, which was presented at a closed-door cabinet session on Thursday, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- Bulgaria is on a U.S. Trade Department "watch list" that will put more pressure on the country to boost protection of intellectual property rights, an department official said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved the sale of stakes in seven big state-owned enterprises in line with pledges made last week by Prime Minister Zhan Videnov.
-- The murder of Andrei Lukanov will not harm the activity of Bulgarian-Russian joint gas company Topenergy, said the head of Bulgaria's state monopolist Bulgargas Petar Sabev.
Loukanov was dropped in July as a Toenergy's board chairman and was replaced by Iliya Pavlov, president of Bulgaria's largest business conglomerate Multigroup.
-- Bulgaria needs some $3 billion to stabilise its largest ailing banks, the Economist magasine said.
Bulgaria could not be able to cover its huge foreign debt payments unless it urgently speeds up privatisation and closes down insolvent banks and debt-ridden firms, the article reads.
PARI

-- Bulgaria's cabinet allowed the country's gas monopolist Bulgargas to give up unprofitable stakes in seven firms and in the Bulgarian-Russian Investment bank, the gas company's executive director Petar Sabev said.

-- Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) plans to cut its record high 300 percent main rate gradually by 50 points per week or a longer period if the International Monetary Fund (IMF) releases a delayed second $115 million tranche to Bulgaria, BNB sources said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to receive the delayed tranche and an an additional IMF credit to support the country's fragile currency, the lev, sources from the BNB said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim is to increase its annual refining volumes to nine million tonnes from 7.5 million tonnes by the year 2005 under a long-term programme, approved by the cabinet.
NOVINAR

-- Bulgarians' lev-denominated deposits in banks declared insolvent by the courts are to be paid one month after court ruling and foreign currency denominated ones two months after it under a draft amendment to the deposit guarantee law.
Currently the state pays up deposits in five banks against which bankruptcy suits have been filed ahead of the possible insolvency rulings.
-- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
